page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps, managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth tests, reaching 7392.89 GB/sec for cached small blocks and up to 464.3 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tests, also place in the top 10% tier. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and gzip compression single-threaded benchmarks falling into the average category.

The hardware profile presents specific tradeoffs. While LLM text generation for medium 7B models ranks in the top tier, text generation for small 135M models is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%. The combination of 3800 GB of local NVMe storage and top-tier database operation benchmarks makes this instance highly suitable for database workloads, Redis deployments, and static web serving. It is also well-suited for software compilation and multi-threaded data processing tasks that leverage its dedicated 64-core ARM architecture.

Benchmarks show top-tier memory bandwidth, multi-core processing, and database operations, though single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation are relatively weaker. This resource density makes the instance highly efficient for multi-threaded workloads. It is best suited for database hosting, Redis deployments, software compilation, and static web serving.
